newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet before holiday- trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet before holiday- trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Wednesday were quiet as the market geared down for the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of this week's sales were on Tuesday at $68.00 per cwt, which was down $2.00 from last week's top price.
Week to date volume in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma areas was 57,600 head confirmed, which included 10,800 formulated cattle to be shipped this week.
Kansas sales were confirmed for the week at 59,900 head including 21,400 head or about 36 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle.
Fed cattle market activity Friday also was seen light, although the threat of a winter storm this weekend in the Panhandle area could generate sales of cattle for quick shipment, market sources said.

A storm was expected to develop over Texas this weekend and move northeastward, generating snow and ice, according to weather forecasters. However, the exact path and severity of the storm remains in question.
